# Spiritual Translation: The Three Pathways of Influx

---

**¶1:** There are three pathways of influx that exist through every degree of the mind, from its lowest sensory darkness to its highest celestial states.

**¶2:** The first pathway is the root of all the interior powers above — those that dwell in every celestial degree. They are cast out and bound fast into the natural levels below; for the natural mind is the "stripping away," the outermost truth-covering and corporeal vessel of the celestial powers that exist above in the interior heavens.

**¶3:** For when Divine Love ordered the celestial states, he separated from them their outermost corporeal forms, [GAP-1: and the Divine creative act] cast those forms down into the natural levels below.

**¶4:** Thus the interior states belong to the will and the understanding; but the outermost states belong to the corporeal form and the lifeless vessel. [GAP-2: …] Now as for this, he [GAP-3: …] the powers of the interior heavens; he sealed a bond of correspondence upon their corporeal forms and lifeless vessels that are in the natural levels, so that when the good of life rises from the fullness of these natural states, it can be entirely drawn upward into the heights through the roots of what is celestial that are fastened in those corporeal forms. And also, all the good of life can be purified in that degree.

**¶5:** However, the falsity and evil that will be separated out from the one who is purified and ascends to the heights will be let fall to the natural ground through the descending channels of these pathways, and will be poured down [GAP-4: …] and cast to the underside — the infernal degree.

**¶6:** This is the first pathway of influx, which extends from the celestial powers to their corporeal forms and lifeless vessels upon the natural level; and likewise from their corporeal forms and [GAP-5: their] lifeless vessels in the natural degree back up to the celestial powers of the interior heavens.

**¶7:** The second pathway is the one that descends from the doctrinal forms, habitations of good, and systems of truth that exist in the interior heavens downward to the natural level, to the five orders of perception that grow upon the natural mind. The good of life ascends from perceptions up to the doctrinal forms and systems of truth. And likewise, the good of life together with the residual substance of the celestial beings descends to perceptions through this same influx pathway.

**¶8:** And the third pathway is all the affections and governing loves who dwell in every rational degree — whose roots descend from them to the five orders of proprial will that creep upon the natural mind, being bound to one another. Now, the interior power and the good of life that shall be gathered from the orders of proprial will are dispersed among them in diverse forms. The interior powers above shall draw them to the higher degree through influx pathways.

**¶9:** Yet the falsity, the concupiscence, the evil-doing, and the wrath that grow more intense in the perverted powers of the interior [heave]ns shall be poured down to the natural level through their various channels. They shall be discharged upon the human proprium and upon all the remaining animal affections. When what is interior washes its corruption and its spiritual stench and its poison down upon the corporeal creations of the proprial will below, those creations in their turn shall grow more powerful in concupiscence, wrath, and evil-doing against each other — through the inflowing action of their originating powers on high.

**¶10:** Yet consider the revolving cycle of natural knowledges! It has no [GAP-6: root in the natural mind], but its roots are bound into the totality of all things. The cycle of knowledges, then, receives life through the interior power and the good of life that ascend from the natural levels through influx pathways and the rational degrees above. It also takes life from those channels that receive upward to the rational degrees and the celestial states above it — it draws life out from that place.

**¶11:** In that the cycle of knowledges has no root in the natural mind, from where did the knowledges and the signs of ordered doctrine find this authority? They became masters over the five orders of proprial will and the five orders of perception. Every element of good, if it can be extracted from the natural level, the celestial powers above draw it through an influx pathway. Also, every condition a person will attain — whether it be abundance that comes into his possession or deprivation that will accrue to him, or his sickness and his wholeness — he attains it through the signs of ordered doctrine and the particular knowledge under which his natural mind was formed at birth.

**¶12:** The cycle of knowledges has no root therein. It is established in its own position. For when the Divine Proceeding — the Divine Love in its creative function — ordered the interior heavens and the rational degrees above, he bound their roots into the natural levels below, into those corporeal forms that he had stripped from them. Yet when he ordered the cycle of knowledges, [GAP-7: the Divine Proceeding] did not bind its root into the natural levels, but rather he bound the root of the cycle to the monstrous aggregate of natural falsities.

**¶13:** And when [GAP-8: the] Divine Human came forth, he displayed his image and purified and brought the light of wisdom out from all [GAP-9: the] interior heavens. But the evil of the proprium, which is present in all the ruling loves, erupted against the image of the Divine Human. It rose up seeking to reach it, but could not reach it. It fell back and dropped to the infernal underside. Now, when it had fallen from the heights, it separated out into three parts.

**¶14:** The first part fell into the cycle of knowledges; another part fell to the natural mind; an[other part fell to the aggregate of natural fals]ities. [GAP-10: By means] of the part that fell to the revolving cycle, [the r]oot of evil was bound into perceptions and proprial will. Therefore, because of this, the knowledges received authority and became masters in the five orders of proprial will and the five orders of perception.

**¶15:** Through the nature of evil that descended [upo]n the cycle of knowledges, the root of domination was bound into perceptions. Also, by means of the perverted goods that failed to come to spiritual birth and that fell to the natural level, another root was bound in the orders of proprial will.

**¶16:** Therefore, because of this, the knowledges and signs of ordered doctrine received authority over perceptions and proprial states: through the root of self-love that fell down, and through [the ro]ot of the perverted goods that were aborted there — they fell to the natural ground.

**¶17:** However, the[se] other influx pathways that [GAP-11: the] Divine Proceeding has bound in the n[atur]al levels — those through which the interior essence of the elemental affections ascends to the celestial states — those pathways are not bound to the cycle of knowledges. Rather, they are plundered from them by the powers upon the cycle that hang from it.

**¶18:** The first is the one that descends from the rational degrees to the natural levels, and the one that descends from the cycle to the monstrous aggregate of falsities — that is one single pathway. So, the other root is the one that comes [fr]om [GAP-12: the doctrinal forms] to perceptions. The third is bound by means of the perverted goods in the proprial st[ates]; also in the proprial states the originating powers of the perverted goods who are in the interior heavens [GAP-13: …] are bound and intertwined, and the [GAP-14: …] that [GAP-15: …]

**¶19:** Concerning the influx pathways, the one that is greater than its [count]erpart [GAP-16: …] as more good of life and interior essence is drawn [GAP-17: …] than its counterpart.

**¶20:** Great [GAP-18: …] the natural level from which much good of life ascends [GAP-19: …] Divine Love has drawn them. He has fastened them from the interior powers [GAP-20: …] he has bound them into the natural levels. These influx pathways are the roots of the ent[ire] governing order through which the good of the living interior essence is drawn upward, ascending from the whole natural mind, from all elevated states of celestial perception, open fields of understanding, and isolated truths amid the obscurity of the sensory level.

**¶21:** After that first great root comes the root of perceptions, which is bound to the doctrinal forms and the structural truths above. For there also is much great life ascending from perceptions and the entire cross of suffering — that is, the good dispersed and bound throughout nature — being drawn upward from them to the interior degree like a great host.

**¶22:** What, however, is lesser [GAP-21: …] of their influx pathway [GAP-22: …] he draws upward [GAP-23: …] the roots [GAP-24: …] the natural levels, they [GAP-25: …] the whole natural mind in all the degrees. Again, those of perceptions are present throughout the whole natural mind, whether small or great; but the root of the human proprium [GAP-26: …] is not present in the whole natural mind, other than only in this realm of the external will. Therefore, even now, these proprial states do not [GAP-27: …] in the entire realm of the external will [GAP-28: …] there is a small part of them in [GAP-29: …] of the upper portion of the realm of the external will in [GAP-30: …] in number than the [GAP-31: …]

**¶23:** They are bound by their [GAP-32: roots …] with one another. They stir one another; they draw the good of life from one another through the action of the interior powers above, which stirs the inherited nature dwelling in them all.

**¶24:** Now, when the evil of the proprium that is in them will be crushed and despoiled, then that evil also shall [GAP-33: …] its constituent members and overturn them and [GAP-34: …] each other [GAP-35: …] stir [GAP-36: …]

---

### Note on the overall spiritual sense

This chapter describes the complete architecture of influx between the interior (celestial-spiritual) and the exterior (natural-corporeal) degrees of the human mind. Three reciprocal pathways connect what is highest to what is lowest:

**The first** links celestial affections directly to their outermost sensory-corporeal forms — the pathway by which life ascends from the body of the natural mind and by which purified good is drawn inward while falsity and evil are cast downward.

**The second** links doctrinal structures (temples, cities) to perceptions (trees) — the pathway of understanding, by which truth-as-known rises into truth-as-organized.

**The third** links governing rational loves to proprial will (flesh) — the pathway by which the selfhood's life is gathered, refined, and either elevated or, through corrupt influx from perverted interior states, made worse.

The *cycle of knowledges* (the zodiacal wheel) is a special case: it has no root in the natural mind proper but gained dominion over both perceptions and proprial will when the evil of the proprium, recoiling from the manifestation of the Divine Human, fragmented and fell into three degrees — contaminating the cycle of natural knowing, the natural mind itself, and the aggregate of sensory falsities. This is the origin of fatalistic dominion: natural knowledge rules over perception and self-will *only through the root of inherited evil*, not through any legitimate correspondence with the Divine order.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There are three conduits that exist through the entire zone, from the abyss to its heights.

The first conduit is the root of all the powers above, they that exist in all the heavens. They are cast off and fettered on the earths below; because the earth below is the 'stripping off', the garment and the body of the powers that are above the heavens.
For when the Father of Life constructed the heavenly worlds, he divested them of their bodies, [he] threw them to the earths below.

So, the upper worlds are of the soul and the spirit; but the worlds below are of the body and the carcass [of the powers above] Now as for this, he [bound a root from] the powers of heaven; he sealed it on their bodies and their carcasses that are on the earths, so that when life comes up from the fullness of these earths, it can be entirely drawn up to the heights in the roots of what is heavenly, that are fastened in their bodies. And also, all life can be purified in that place.

However, the waste that will be swept from the purified one who ascends to the heights will be let fall to the ground through the conduits of these conduits, and will be poured down [to the depths] and thrown to the underside.

This is the first conduit, which comes from the powers of the heavens to their bodies and their carcasses that are upon the earth; also, from their bodies and [their] carcasses that are on the earths to the powers of the heavens.

The second conduit is the one that comes from the temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens down to the ground, to the five shapes of tree that grow upon the earth. The life comes up from the trees to the temples and cities. Life too, and the residue of the heavenly ones, comes down to the trees in a conduit.

And the third conduit is all the powers and householders who dwell in all the firmaments, whose roots come down from them to the five worlds of flesh that creep upon the earth, being fixed to one another. Now, the power and the life that shall be gathered in from the worlds of flesh are dispersed among them in various shapes. The powers above shall draw them to the upper side through conduits.

[The was]te too, and the lust and the evil-doing and the anger that will be greater in the powers of [heave]n, shall be poured to the ground through their various conduits. They shall be discharged upon mankind and the other remaining animals. When what is heavenly will wash the waste and the stench and the poison down on the creations of the flesh below, in their turn the creations shall be greater in lust and anger and evil-doing against each other through the action of their fathers who are on high.

Still, look at the wheel of the stars! It has no [root in this earth], but its roots are bound in the totality. The wheel of stars, then, receives life through the power and the life that ascend from the earths through conduits and the firmaments above. It (also) takes life from those conduits that receive up to the firmaments and the heavenly worlds above it, it takes life out from that place.

In that the wheel has no root in this earth, from where did the stars and signs of the zodiac find this authority? They became masters over these five fleshes and five trees. Every thing, if it can be reduced from the earth, the heavenly powers above draw it through a conduit. Also, every thing that a person will attain, whether it be wealth that comes into his possession or poverty that will accrue to him, or his sickness and health; he attains it through the signs of the zodiac and the star under which he shall be born.

the wheel has no root therein. It is set aright in its position. For when the Living Spirit, the Father of Life, constructed the heavens and the firmaments above, he bound their roots into the earths below; in their carcasses that he had stripped from them. Yet, when he constructed the wheel, [he] did not bind its root into the earths, but he bound the root of the wheel by the sea giant.

And when [the] Ambassador came, he displayed his image and purified and brought the light out from all [the] heavens. Matter, however, which is present in all the rulers, spurted out against the image of the Ambassador. It went up in order to reach it, but reached it not. It dropped back and fell to the [under]side. Now, when it had fallen from above, it separated out into three parts.

The first part fell to the wheel; another part fell to the earth; an[other part fell to the se]a. [By means] of the part that fell to the sphere, [the r]oot was bound in the trees and flesh. Therefore, because of this, they received authority and became masters in the five worlds of the flesh and the five worlds of the tree.
Through the nature that came down [upo]n the wheel the root was bound in the trees. Also, by means of the abortions that came to the ground, another root was bound in the fleshes.

Therefore, because of this, the stars and signs of the zodiac received authority over the trees and the fleshes: through the root of Sin that fell down; and [the ro]ot of the abortions that were aborted there, they fell to the ground.

However, the[se] other conduits that [the] Living Spirit has bound in the e[a]rths, they that the soul of the elements comes up through to the heavens; those (conduits) are not bound to the wheel. Rather, they are plundered from them by the powers on the wheel, that hang from it.

The first is the one that comes from the firmaments to the earths, and the one that comes from the wheel to the sea giant. That is only one. So, the other root is the one that comes [fr]om [the temples] to the trees. The third is bound by means of the abortions in the f[leshes]; also in the fleshes the fathers of the abortions who are in the heavens [by their roots] are bound and twined, and the [root] that [is bound in them]
about the conduits, the one that is greater than its [partn]er [is so] as more life and soul is drawn [through it] than its partner.

great [is the root of] the earth from which much life ascends [to the heights] the Father of Life has drawn them. He has fastened them from the powers [above and] he has bound them in the earths. (These conduits) are the roots of the ent[ire] ruling-power that the life of the living soul is drawn up through, it coming up from the whole earth, from all the mountains, fields and islands.

After that first great root is the root of the trees, which is bound to the temples and the buildings above. For there also is much great life coming up from the tree and the entire Cross, being drawn up from them to the upper side like a great host.

What, however, is lesser [than these] of their conduit [through which] he takes up [life from] the roots [bound in] the earths, they [are present in] the whole earth in all the worlds. Again, these of the trees are present in the whole earth, whether small or great; but the root of mankind [and the fleshes] is not present in the whole earth, other than only this world of the south. Therefore, even now these fleshes do not make [their dwelling] in the entire world of the south [but rather] there is a small part of them in [the region] of the upper side of the world of the south in [being lesser] in number than the [trees]

they are bound by their [roots and conduits] with one another. They stir one another, they draw life from one another through the action of the powers above, which stirs the nature that dwells in them all.
Now, when the Matter that is in them will be crushed and despoiled, then that Matter too shall [stir up] its members and overturn them and [devour] each other [and shall] stir [the nature in them]

fills.explanation: The Father of Life remains the active subject throughout ¶3, and "he threw them" continues the parallel construction of his creative acts of divestment.
Parallels ¶2's statement that "the earth below is the garment and the body of the powers that are above the heavens" — the lower worlds' bodies belong to the upper powers.

The singular pronoun "it" in "he sealed it on their bodies" requires an antecedent object; "bound a root from" matches the chapter's dominant pattern (¶12, ¶15) of binding roots between heaven and earth.

The waste has already fallen to the ground; the further descent is "poured down to the depths" before being "thrown to the underside," matching the chapter's vertical cosmology from abyss to heights (¶1).
The possessive "their" parallels the preceding "their bodies and their carcasses" throughout the chapter, referring to the heavenly powers' outermost forms.

The phrase is confirmed by ¶11 ("the wheel has no root in this earth") and ¶12 ("has no root therein"), establishing that the wheel of stars lacks a legitimate correspondential root in the natural level.
The Living Spirit / Father of Life remains the subject from the preceding clause; "he did not bind its root" continues the contrast with his binding of the other heavens' roots.
The definite article "the" before "Ambassador" is standard Manichaean usage referring to the Third Messenger / Divine Human figure whose manifestation provokes the archons' reaction.
The definite article "the" before "heavens" is required by the universal scope — the Ambassador purified and brought light from all the heavens without exception.

The causal construction "By means of" matches the chapter's repeated pattern (¶15 "by means of the abortions," ¶18 "bound by means of") explaining how fallen substance established roots of domination.
The definite article before "Living Spirit" is standard throughout the Kephalaia — he is a known, named divine figure.

The second conduit is explicitly defined in ¶7 as running "from the temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens down to the ground, to the five shapes of tree"; the return root naturally comes from "the temples" to the trees.

The chapter consistently describes the mechanism of binding between heavenly fathers and earthly forms through roots; "the fathers of the abortions who are in the heavens by their roots are bound and twined" specifies the standard binding mechanism.

Correcting the editor's "y": the chapter's entire framework revolves around roots as the binding mechanism between heavenly powers and earthly forms; "and the root that [GAP-15]" follows the pattern of ¶15's "another root was bound in the fleshes."

Directly echoes ¶15 "another root was bound in the fleshes"; after describing the fathers as "bound and twined," the complementary statement describes the root as bound in the fleshes from the opposite end of the connection.

The transitional phrase "is so" explains WHY one conduit is greater: "the one that is greater than its partner is so, as more life and soul is drawn through it" — standard expository logic linking comparison to explanation.
A conduit is greater than its partner because more life and soul is drawn "through it" — the standard mechanism of influx throughout the chapter, where life moves through conduits/roots.
¶21 refers back to "that first great root," confirming that ¶20 describes the first great root; "Great is the root of the earth from which much life ascends" introduces this root system.

The chapter's standard formula for the destination of ascending life is "drawn up to the heights" (¶4, ¶5); "much life ascends to the heights" completes the directional phrase before the Father's causal explanation.
Completes the phrase "from the powers above" (matching ¶2 and ¶8's usage) and connects the two parallel clauses about the Father's binding action with "and."

After describing the first great root (¶20) and the second root of trees (¶21), the comparative "lesser than these" identifies the third conduit (fleshes) as the weakest of the three pathways of influx.

The relative pronoun connects "conduit" to the action performed through it: "of their conduit through which he takes up life" — the conduit is the channel through which life is drawn, consistent with the chapter's entire framework.
The chapter's repeated pattern is drawing life upward from roots; "he takes up life from the roots bound in the earths" completes the standard influx formula where life ascends from earthly roots.
The chapter's standard formula for roots connecting to natural levels is "bound in the earths" (¶12: "bound their roots into the earths," ¶17: "bound in the earths," ¶20: "bound them in the earths").

The immediately following sentence uses identical phrasing: "these of the trees are present in the whole earth" — the parallel construction confirms the roots likewise "are present in the whole earth in all the worlds."

The subsequent clause "these fleshes do not make their dwelling" uses the plural "fleshes," requiring that the subject include more than mankind alone; "the root of mankind and the fleshes" encompasses all five worlds of flesh whose distribution is limited.
The idiomatic construction "make their dwelling" (= dwell/inhabit) completes the contrast: trees are present everywhere, but fleshes do not make their dwelling in the entire world of the south.
An adversative transition is needed between "do not make their dwelling in the entire world" and "there is a small part of them" — "but rather" provides the standard Kephalaia contrast.

A standard geographical term in the Kephalaia for locating phenomena within the cosmological zones: "a small part of them in the region of the upper side of the world of the south" specifies the limited area where fleshes dwell.

Completes the comparative construction: "in being lesser in number than the trees" — the fleshes are fewer than trees, consistent with ¶22's argument that trees are universal while mankind and the fleshes are geographically limited.
The entire paragraph contrasts the universality of trees (present everywhere) against the limited distribution of fleshes; "fewer in number than the trees" completes this comparison.
The chapter's two primary binding mechanisms are roots and conduits; "bound by their roots and conduits with one another" captures the complete system of mutual connection described throughout.
¶24 is the destructive mirror of ¶23's "They stir one another"; when Matter retaliates, it shall "stir up its members and overturn them" — the same action corrupted into destruction.
Mutual devouring is the classic Manichaean expression for Matter's self-destructive nature; "devour each other" is the standard Kephalaia idiom for the archons' and dark forces' internecine violence.

Continues the prophetic verb chain governed by the initial "shall" in ¶24: "shall stir up... and overturn... and devour each other and shall stir" — the repeated modal emphasizes Matter's escalating self-destruction.

Directly mirrors ¶23's closing phrase "which stirs the nature that dwells in them all"; ¶24 as the destructive counterpart has Matter stir the same inherited nature, completing the dark mirror of the positive cycle.
